summary.text: Gravitational time dilation is an actual difference in elapsed time between observers at different distances from a gravitating mass.
The closer a clock is to the source of gravitation, the slower its time passes, and it speeds up as the clock moves farther away.
Effects on Earth are tiny, but large enough that the atomic clocks on GPS satellites had to be permanently corrected.

facts.label: At the Sun's surface
facts.value: A clock loses about 66.4 seconds in a year

facts.label: Smallest height seen
facts.value: Verified in the lab for differences under one metre

items.prompt: Two identical atomic clocks start together, then one sits on a mountaintop and the other at sea level for years. Which one has counted more time?

options.label: The sea level clock, being closer to Earth
Neither, since both are the same make
The mountaintop clock, being farther from Earth
The one that was started first

items.explain: Clocks farther from massive bodies run more quickly, and clocks close to them run more slowly.

items.prompt: Engineers building a satellite navigation system correct the clocks on the satellites in advance. Why bother?

options.label: Orbit changes their clock rate enough to matter
Space dust slowly damages the clocks aboard
Ground clocks are always less accurate there
Satellites move too slowly to be tracked well

items.explain: The effect is significant enough that the satellites' atomic clocks were permanently corrected.

items.prompt: An observer deep in a gravitational well, with slowed time, measures how fast light travels right where they are. What do they get?

options.label: A speed lower than usual
A speed higher than usual
The usual speed of light
A speed that varies with their clock

items.explain: The speed of light in a locale is always equal to c according to the observer who is there.

items.prompt: Why is an accelerating spaceship connected to the slowing of clocks near a planet?

options.label: Both involve friction against a surrounding medium
Accelerated frames are equivalent to a gravitational field of the same strength
Spaceships can only accelerate near planets
Planets and ships both heat their clocks

items.explain: By the equivalence principle, accelerated reference frames are physically equivalent to a gravitational field, so the time dilation appears in both.

items.prompt: Over Earth's whole 4.6-billion-year history, how does time at the planet's core compare with time at its surface?

options.label: The core is about 2.5 years younger
The core is about 2.5 years older
They are identical to the second
The core is about 2.5 hours older

items.explain: Deeper in the gravitational well time runs slower, so relative to Earth's age the core is in effect 2.5 years younger than the surface.

items.prompt: A source emits light of constant frequency from near a very dense body. How does a far-off fixed observer see that light?

options.label: At a higher frequency, bluer than emitted
At exactly the frequency it was emitted
At a lower frequency, shifted toward red
As a steady beam with no frequency

items.explain: The closer the emitter is to the gravitating body, the more its time is slowed, so the observed light has a lower, more redshifted frequency.
